items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023
items.q: I did the 1983 “Miles and Gil Tour Japan.” And I also played on the last recording of Miles Davis and Quincy Jones in Montreux, Switzerland, 1991.

ctx.x: Talk about, let’s talk about Gil Evans a little more. I was having a — reading something and trying to write something about the major innovators in jazz history and the fact that the majority of them are African-American. So then I went like well who’s the first white musician that seemed to make a significant contribution to changing jazz. And I thought of Gil Evans, I thought of Bix, but I thought of Gil Evans as a writer. Would you agree with that?

I would totally agree with that, yes. We’re talking about “Porgy & Bess,” “Miles Ahead,” “Sketches in Spain” particularly. “Sketches in Spain,” Gil Evans arranging for Miles Davis. Now I did the 1983 “Miles and Gil Tour Japan.” And I also played on the last recording of Miles Davis and Quincy Jones in Montreux, Switzerland, 1991. Miles passed away about three weeks later. But you know Miles was certainly a big influence. And Gil Evans was my musical father for his last fifteen years. We played, among other things…
